headline: Argentine Central Bank Intervenes as Brazilian Real Depreciation Weighs on Parity
summary: The Brazilian real approached 6 per US dollar, driving Argentina's bilateral real exchange rate down 13.7% in less than a month. The Central Bank of the Argentine Republic continued purchasing foreign currency despite official exchange rate increases.
why: Brazil is Argentina's main trading partner; exchange rate swings between the real and peso directly affect South American trade balances and foreign exchange reserves.

impacts.name: Argentine Peso
impacts.why: Sharp depreciation in the Brazilian real puts pressure on Argentina's foreign exchange policy and bilateral trade competitiveness.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Rapid depreciation of the Brazilian real weakened Argentina's bilateral exchange rate competitiveness.
